Hey /fitness/,

I've been lifting recreationally for a few years. I started out not really caring what I was doing, so long as I kept a sub-12% bf. My weight plateau's fairly naturally at 180lbs, though I do have Graves Disease (hyperthyroid) which is in remission after years being on meds (never wanted to have it removed/destroyed). I've been as high as 200lbs during a bulk, and as low as 170 during a cut.

I'm on a modified 5x5 SL program, doing AxBxAxBxAxB etc., and my major lifts are as follows:

Squat: 235 x 5 reps (plateau'ed there on purpose) Deadlift: 255 x 5 reps (I know, my pull sucks, I'm working on it) Bench: 185 x 5 reps OHP: 135 x 5 reps I also run 3 mile every other day with my wife.

Ok, on to the problem: on days when I work out, I have trouble sleeping that night. I work out from 3:30pm-5pm every day, and occasionally I drink green tea prior to working out. Has anyone else had issues of trouble sleeping on workout days? Any ideas on things that help get at least 8 hours?
My first thought is that the green tea might have caffeine in it. But I didn't think it would have that much in it. Have you tried not drinking green tea to see what happens?

It does, quite a bit, but I usually head to bed around 9:30pm... it should well and truly not impact my sleep then, surely?

It's one solution, and I'm willing to try it.
It does seem like a long time, but who knows? Does anything else change in your diet on lifting days?

No, I eat the same thing every day with very little variation, at about 3000 calories maintenance.

Oats & berries for breakfast Homemade chilli for lunch Chicken and vegetables for dinner
I have no idea what else it could be.

I am very sensitive to caffeine and if I have any after 12:00/noon, then I have difficulty falling asleep. If you do not consume much caffeinated emerges then you might be more sensitive as well. In the past I have had difficulties falling asleep in general and have found tryptophan to work for me... Not sure if it is the placebo effect or not, but... hey, it works for me! If you have a really early bedtime, then it could also play into the equation, but if you're going to sleep at ten or later then it should not. Think about any supplements that you might take or after gym recovery shakes that you might take as well. Keep us updated; sleep is important for the recovery process and life in general!
Thanks a lot. I might try tryptophan. I am not currently on any supps and haven't been for the 12 months. Have you tried melatonin or other supp?
I tried melatonin and valerian root, but for me it really made no difference, but a lifting buddy of mine takes it and it seems to work for him.
